name: "Stone Cold" Steve Austin

portrays.note: The XCW (X-Treme) wing's own Monday Night Malice of 4 January 2002 and PPV update of 15 January 2002 stage this character under the real performer's own ring name, per the per-promotion portrayal rule.

caption: The real wrestler as an XCW character in January 2002: a stunner-machine who beats Rob Van Dam to a pulp, targets the Television Title and tags with Mikey Whipwreck against Shane Douglas and Vader.
notes: Played in XCW (X-Treme) by one handler in two roleplays posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy for critique (msg_ids gNpDDJzxahYJ, 10 January 2002, and -MJ3c_RhNgMJ, 12 January 2002), served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/critique-stone-cold-steve-austin-2002-01-10.html and /promotions/rspwf/archive/rp-critique-again-stone-cold-steve-austin-2002-01-12.html. The XCW (X-Treme) wing's own Monday Night Malice of 4 January 2002 has Austin ambushing Rob Van Dam dressed as a Rasta man, and its PPV update of 15 January 2002 books Rob Van Dam against him for the XCW Television Title. Billed as a real wrestler playing himself in a real-roster federation.

name: Rob Van Dam

portrays.note: The XCW (X-Treme) wing's own Monday Night Malice of 4 and 28 January 2002 and its New Year's Brawl of 21 January 2002 stage this character under the real performer's own ring name, per the per-promotion portrayal rule.

notes: Known from one post to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy (15 January 2002), served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/critique-rvd-flash-2002-01-15.html: Rob Van Dam, lifting 1,000 pounds on a leg press in a Battle Creek gym, tells Steve Austin that at New Years Brawl he will win their Last Man Standing match, rips him for taking orders from Chad Costello and ends by asking readers how bad he is.
caption: The real wrestler as an XCW character in January 2002: the Television champion, feuding with Steve Austin into their title match at New Year's Brawl.

name: Tommy Dreamer

portrays.note: The XCW (X-Treme) wing's own Monday Night Malice of 28 January 2002, its Wednesday Night Hardcore of May and June 2002 and its Beach Blast of 16 June 2002 stage this character under the real performer's own ring name, per the per-promotion portrayal rule.

notes: Known from one post to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy (21 January 2002), served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/critique-tommy-dreamer-post-2002-01-21.html: Tommy Dreamer, in a bleak dressing room to Alice in Chains, tells the camera of his years in ECW and the WWF, declares he is in XCW to stay and promises Jake Roberts a knife to the head on Friday Night X-Treme; Beulah McGillicutty then asks him which of two outfits he likes best.
caption: The real wrestler as an XCW character in 2002: the Innovator of Violence, starting with a promo against Jake Roberts and later in a feud with Raven for the United States title.
